title: Bridging the green attitude-behavior gap: Development and validation of the multidimensional sense of environmental responsibility scale.
abstract: The green attitude-behavior gap remains a barrier to sustainability initiatives in higher education. To distinguish the sense of environmental responsibility (SOER) from broader environmental responsibility, this study developed and validated the multidimensional Sense of Environmental Responsibility Scale (SOERS) among Chinese university students. Across three studies, principal component analysis suggested, and confirmatory factor analysis and item response theory provided further support for, an 11-item, three-factor representation comprising cognition, affective response, and behavioral intention. The scale showed good internal consistency, test-retest reliability, discriminant validity, and concurrent criterion validity. Item response theory supported satisfactory item performance, and scalar measurement invariance was established across gender; female students reported higher SOER levels. The SOERS offers a psychometrically sound tool for assessing individuals' sense of environmental responsibility and provides a measurement foundation for future intervention research examining whether changes in SOER are associated with a narrower attitude-behavior gap.
